children: Canadian National Railway

is building on higher freight volumes and productivity gains, but a labor outage at a Prince Rupert export facility is affecting its fourth-quarter numbers, President and CEO Tracy Robinson said at the Scotiabank Transportation and Industrials Conference.

Robinson said the railway’s commercial push has generated CAD 300 million in incremental revenue so far this year, while its operational improvement program has produced CAD 120 million in structural cost benefits. She also outlined growth opportunities in energy, potash and intermodal traffic heading into 2027.

children: CN reaffirmed its earnings-per-share growth guidance in the third quarter and pointed to the top end of its range, Robinson said. Over time, she said, the railroad can produce high-single-digit to low-double-digit EPS growth in an environment like the current one.
Productivity and Commercial Gains
Employee productivity rose 8% and locomotive productivity increased 6% over the past nine months, Robinson said. CN also recorded its best quarterly fuel efficiency in the third quarter.

In the western corridor, where CN moves its highest density of traffic, third-quarter volumes rose 4% while car velocity increased 3%, she said. The company is using capacity created by earlier investments to move more freight and improve operating leverage.

On the commercial side, Robinson said CN’s “boots-on-the-ground” program sends employees out to find freight that can fill available space on existing trains or routes. The opportunities range from a handful of railcars to unit trains, and some are short-lived while others can become recurring business.

“It is just a kind of cadence of new business that fits our network, that we can service well,” Robinson said. She added that the program has been generating about CAD 100 million a quarter in new business.

Grain has been a strong contributor to volume and market-share gains, Robinson said. She also cited growth in natural gas liquids, refined products, automotive, domestic intermodal and metals, with volumes in those categories up between 4% and 17% so far this year.
Growth Plans and Capital Spending

For 2027, Robinson pointed to the opening of the Strathcona Meota crude oil facility, additional natural gas liquids fractionation capacity, the second phase of a Toronto refined-fuel facility and the expected arrival of BHP potash volumes in the second half of the year. Automotive plants returning from retooling and domestic intermodal demand could also contribute, she said.

Robinson said a three-year investment cycle increased western network capacity by 25%. CN expects to meet its CAD 2.8 billion capital program this year and can accommodate further growth without a proportional increase in capital spending, she said. Free cash flow rose 25% through the first nine months of the year.

Capital spending of roughly 15% to 17% of revenue is a sustainable normalized range for a period of time, Robinson said. She also said CN does not expect to change its financial strategy or capital-allocation priorities when Jamie Lockwood becomes chief financial officer in February.
Union Pacific Agreement and Prince Rupert

CN is finalizing an agreement with Union Pacific that would give CN access toward Mexico and make some CN capacity available to Union Pacific, Robinson said. CN is also working with Mexican railroad Ferromex on market plans.

Robinson said the agreement is independent of the outcome of a proposed merger involving Union Pacific. CN has agreed not to oppose the merger but will participate in the regulatory process to support its agreement, she said.

At Prince Rupert, Robinson highlighted the recently opened CANXPORT facility, which transfers commodities from railcars into empty containers, and an expected expansion of natural gas liquids export capacity. CN anticipates carload traffic will account for 60% of the port’s volume by 2030, she said.

Robinson said a labor outage at the Trigon facility, which handles natural gas liquids and export coal, is affecting fourth-quarter numbers that had been at or above plan. She said discussions were underway and expressed hope for a quick resolution.
About Canadian National Railway

Canadian National Railway, commonly known as CN, is a North American transportation and logistics company that operates a freight rail network connecting Canada's Atlantic, Pacific and Gulf coasts with the United States. Its network serves customers across Canada and the U.S. Midwest and South. CN transports a range of commodities and manufactured goods, including intermodal shipments, grain and fertilizers, petroleum and chemicals, forest products, metals and minerals, and finished vehicles. The company also provides services such as rail-connected logistics and supply-chain solutions.
